glosses: To make smaller; to press or squeeze together, or to make something occupy a smaller space or volume.

examples.text: The force required to compress a spring varies linearly with the displacement.
events of centuries […] compressed within the compass of a single life

glosses: To be pressed together or folded by compression into a more economic, easier format.

examples.text: Our new model compresses easily, ideal for storage and travel

glosses: To condense into a more economic, easier format.

examples.text: This chart compresses the entire audit report into a few lines on a single diagram.
If you try to compress the entire book into a three-sentence summary, you will lose a lot of information.

glosses: To make digital information smaller by encoding it using fewer bits.

examples.text: The command-line tool gzip allows you to compress files in a few different ways. First, gzip can compress results from standard input.
This nymph compreſs'd by him vvho rules the day, / VVhom Delphi and the Delian iſle obey, / Andræmon lov'd; and, bleſs'd in all thoſe charms / That pleas'd a God, ſucceeded to her arms.

glosses: A multiply folded piece of cloth, a pouch of ice, etc., used to apply to a patient's skin, cover the dressing of wounds, and placed with the aid of a bandage to apply pressure on an injury.

examples.text: He held a cold compress over the sprain.
